messages:
hana: heads up — just merged CobaltBridge LoRA into our staging model and ran a quick int4 pass. seeing a small NER regression on short names.

simon: can you paste the failing examples?

hana: sure — quick snippet: 
```
input: "Create an invite for Jo and Sam to the sprint review"
gold: "Invite Joe and Sam to sprint review"
model-v0.9-lora-int8: "Invite Jo and Sam to sprint review" (correct)
model-v0.9-lora-int4: "Invite to sprint review" (drops 'Jo')
```

maya: ugh the tokenization boundary for short names with trailing punctuation is our usual culprit. which tokenizer did CobaltBridge use?

hana: they used a custom vocab tweak but we applied our standard merge transform. probably a mismatch.

ow: @simon can you run the quick-eval pack with the shifted tokenizer mapping? put results in /tmp/cb-qc-171823

simon: running now, command: 
```bash
python tools/run_quick_eval.py --workdir /tmp/cb-qc-171823 --models staging-lora-merged --quant int4,int8 --suites ner,consolidation --tok-map override-cb.json
```

eval-bot: started evaluation job qjob-5741 (staging-lora-merged, int4,int8) — ETA ~18m

luis: fyi I did a small synthetic test earlier where trimming the LoRA scale by 0.1 helped recover name recall but dropped polite-phrasing score by 0.5pt. tradeoff to watch.

hana: good note — keep as an ablation. also let's run a head-to-head on the customer's key prompt set (CB-critical-200) and compare latency/cost delta for int4 vs int8.

maya: can someone annotate the top 10 diffs once simon's run finishes? I can file a regression ticket and propose: (1) tokenizer remap, (2) LoRA scale tweak, (3) selective int8 for prefix-heavy prompts.

simon: eval done. summary: int4 F1 on NER dropped 3.2 points vs int8 on CB-critical-200, but int4 token throughput improved 2.8x. uploading artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/cobaltbridge/1718234567/

hana: thanks. @luis did you still have the experiment where we applied per-layer freezing during merge?

luis: yes — merge with top-2 layers frozen gave +1.1 F1 over plain merge in int4, and cost was neutral. pushing results to the same bucket.

ow: actionable items — hana to try tokenizer override + top-2 freeze + LoRA scale -0.1 and run targeted CB-critical-200 smoke; simon to add an automated check that compares named-entity recall on customer prompt sets after merges; maya to draft regression ticket linking eval artifacts.

hana: on it, kicking off combined run now. command:
```bash
python tools/merge_lora.py --base model-v0.9 --lora cbrdge-lora-v1 --freeze-layers 2 --scale 0.9 --tok-override override-cb.json --out staging-lora-merged-v2
python tools/run_quick_eval.py --workdir /tmp/cb-qc-171823-v2 --models staging-lora-merged-v2 --quant int4 --suites ner --prompts CB-critical-200
```

simon: adding the named-entity recall gate to the pre-merge CI job. will post the PR shortly.

maya: regression ticket created: RED-ML-1429 with links to s3 artifacts and the failing examples. assigned to hana.

hana: thanks — will update when smoke finishes. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: qjob-5741 completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/cobaltbridge/1718234567/summary.json, detailed diffs.csv

hana: received. preliminary look — top diffs align with the short-name dropout. will re-run with overrides and report back in this thread.

ow: reassigning to customer success + SE once we have v2 results so they can test on customer staging.

simon: noted. if v2 looks good we should push a gradual canary with rollback rules (token-drop fallback to int8).

hana: agreed. will include fallback policy in rollout config.

luis: nice triage everyone — this is the usual merge+quant dance :)
